author: harness:claude-code

patch.value: Attested context reads: an assembly records the inputs that produced it and can be reproduced and independently checked, so the observation half of a decision has the same standing as the mutation half

The project has made writes provable and left reads unaccounted for. Every mutation is hash-chained into an immutable stream, pm-3z0k exports a detached proof a third party can verify, pm-u14c adds per-entry principal signatures, and pm-w7ccmv holds the outcome that every mutation is immutably recorded and independently verifiable. Nothing gives the same standing to what an agent actually consumed.

A context assembly is a lossy, ranked, budget-truncated projection over the record. Two invocations may legitimately differ: relevance scoring reads recency, the graph changes underneath, the token budget forces a different truncation point, extension state alters the candidate set. None of that is recorded. After the fact there is no way to answer what an agent saw, and therefore no way to answer whether a decision was reasonable given what it had, or whether two agents that disagreed were even looking at the same thing.

Three places this is already load-bearing rather than theoretical.

Post-hoc review of agent work. The immutable record answers what was written and by whom, with the model resolvable once pm-ffz0a9 lands. It cannot answer what was in front of the agent when it wrote it. An audit that can see the action and not the observation is reading half a decision.

Training and evaluation. pm-li2fj5 requires the observation to be a bounded projection with withheld grading fields, and pm-qd6gvf requires each trajectory step to carry the observation boundary in force. Neither can hold if the assembly is not reproducible: an unreproducible observation makes the whole trajectory unreproducible regardless of how sound the mutation record beneath it is. This is the read-side half that the write-side proof programme does not cover.

Disagreement between concurrent agents. In a fleet, two agents reaching different conclusions is either a real difference of judgement or a difference in what the context engine handed them, and today those two cases are indistinguishable.

What an attested read has to establish, in increasing strength. That the assembly is reproducible: the same recorded state, budget and scoring version produce byte-identical output, which requires the assembly to be a pure function of declared inputs and is the same determinism property pm-rbcvt2 establishes for workspace construction. That the inputs are named: the envelope records the record version or point-in-time anchor, the scoring version, the budget, and the candidate-set filters, so the assembly can be replayed later against the same anchor. And that a third party can check it: a compact digest over the assembly plus its declared inputs, verifiable against the history the way pm-3z0k's bundle is, so an observation claim can be confirmed without trusting the claimant.

The hard constraint is that this must not make reads expensive. The whole point of the context surface is that it is the cheap call an agent makes constantly. Attestation therefore has to be opt-in per call or per workspace, and the digest has to be computable as a by-product of an assembly that already happened rather than as a second pass over the record.

Boundaries. pm-4k6b owns the relevance algorithm and pm-vvib the memory architecture; this item does not choose or change scoring, it requires that whatever scoring is chosen be versioned and its output reproducible. pm-5gf0xf owns workspace-level point-in-time projection and supplies the anchor this reads against. pm-3z0k and pm-u14c own the write-side proof this is the counterpart to. Named as an open question in horizon K on pm-doxj and filed so the horizon has an owner rather than a note.

The same recorded state, token budget and scoring version produce a byte-identical context assembly, proven by a determinism test and a deliberate-nondeterminism negative control; An assembly envelope names the point-in-time anchor, the scoring version, the token budget and the candidate-set filters that produced it; An assembly can be replayed later from its declared inputs and shown to match what the record supported at that anchor; A compact digest over the assembly and its declared inputs is independently verifiable against history without trusting the producer; Attestation is opt-in per call or per workspace and its cost is a by-product of an assembly that already ran, with the default read path measurably unchanged; Scoring changes bump a declared scoring version so an older attested assembly is never silently reinterpreted under newer scoring

message: Filed to give horizon K's second open question an owner. Duplicate check: searched reproducible/attestation/read-proof and context/determinism; pm-3z0k and pm-u14c are write-side proof, pm-rbcvt2 is workspace-construction determinism, pm-5gf0xf is the point-in-time anchor, pm-4k6b and pm-vvib own scoring and memory architecture. None covers reproducibility or attestation of the assembled read.
